finding.message: src/presentation/order.controller.ts (presentation) skips layers to import src/persistence/order-read.repository.ts (persistence)

answer.explanation: OrderController is in the presentation layer. It imports OrderReadRepository from the persistence layer (order.controller.ts:2), injects it through its constructor (line 7), and calls reads.findSummaries directly in list() (lines 14-15). Writes go through the business layer: place() delegates to OrderService.place (line 11). Reads skip the business layer and reach persistence directly. FF-S03 flags this edge because a layer may depend only on the layer directly below it, and presentation is two layers above persistence. Only the read path breaks this, so it looks like a read-side shortcut. No comment in the code explains it.

OrderController in the presentation layer imports OrderReadRepository from the persistence layer (src/presentation/order.controller.ts:2), receives it by constructor injection (line 7) and calls findSummaries directly in list() (line 15). Its other path, place(), correctly goes through the business layer's OrderService (line 11). This read path skips the business layer entirely, so the presentation layer depends directly on persistence. FF-S03 forbids that kind of layer skip. It reads like a CQRS-style read shortcut, but no project text marks it as an accepted read-side bypass. The README describes the service as three layers (presentation, business, persistence), and this edge goes around the middle one. The fix is small and local: add a query method to the business layer (for example on OrderService or a dedicated read service) that wraps findSummaries, and have the controller inject only business-layer types.
